Previously, we saw flakes like `ERROR: unsupported comparison operator: <string> = <timetz>` occurring in the rsw because at times, we were indexing a column name in a map without any guards. This meant that if any improperly quoted column name was being looked up in the map, we would just return the default for that key not existing in our map (0). This caused us to refer an arbitrary column's values when validating FK constraints, causing a mismatch that we see above.

We now have checks to guard us from making this mistake again, along with proper quotes around column names.

In addition, alter FK statements and inserts in the same explicit txn did not bode well - as the query to get our `fkConstraints` relied on the `crdb_internal.is_constraint_active` builtin, which does not work in the legacy schema changer: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/120702. In this case, we do not need the builtin to filter for our FK constraints.

Epic: none
Fixes: #119288

Release note: None

We aren't getting the correct `fkConstraints` https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/82e2be01134e43a010972eda547290cdb662fdaf/pkg/workload/schemachange/error_screening.go#L1064 in an explicit txn.

Repro: 

```
create table t(i int, j int unique);

create table t2(q int, w int unique);

BEGIN;

alter table t add constraint aa foreign key (j) references public.t2 (w);

SELECT array[parent.table_schema, parent.table_name, quote_ident(parent.column_name), quote_ident(child.column_name)]
		  FROM (
		        SELECT conname, conkey, confkey, conrelid, confrelid
		          FROM pg_constraint
		         WHERE contype = 'f'
		           AND conrelid = 'public.t'::REGCLASS::INT8
		       ) AS con
			JOIN ( SELECT CONSTRAINT_NAME from information_schema.table_constraints 
				      WHERE table_schema ='public' AND
								    table_name='t' AND
										(crdb_internal.is_constraint_active('public.t', constraint_name) = true)
           ) AS tc ON conname = tc.CONSTRAINT_NAME
		  JOIN (
		        SELECT column_name, ordinal_position, column_default
		          FROM information_schema.columns
		         WHERE table_schema = 'public'
		           AND table_name = 't'
		       ) AS child ON conkey[1] = child.ordinal_position
		  JOIN (
		        SELECT pc.oid,
		               cols.table_schema,
		               cols.table_name,
		               cols.column_name,
		               cols.ordinal_position
		          FROM pg_class AS pc
		          JOIN pg_namespace AS pn ON pc.relnamespace = pn.oid
		          JOIN information_schema.columns AS cols ON (pc.relname = cols.table_name AND pn.nspname = cols.table_schema)
		       ) AS parent ON (
		                       con.confkey[1] = parent.ordinal_position
		                       AND con.confrelid = parent.oid
		                      )
		 WHERE child.column_name != 'rowid';
<--- nothing returned here

COMMIT;

SELECT array[parent.table_schema, parent.table_name, quote_ident(parent.column_name), quote_ident(child.column_name)]
		  FROM (
		        SELECT conname, conkey, confkey, conrelid, confrelid
		          FROM pg_constraint
		         WHERE contype = 'f'
		           AND conrelid = 'public.t'::REGCLASS::INT8
		       ) AS con
			JOIN ( SELECT CONSTRAINT_NAME from information_schema.table_constraints 
				      WHERE table_schema ='public' AND
								    table_name='t' AND
										(crdb_internal.is_constraint_active('public.t', constraint_name) = true)
           ) AS tc ON conname = tc.CONSTRAINT_NAME
		  JOIN (
		        SELECT column_name, ordinal_position, column_default
		          FROM information_schema.columns
		         WHERE table_schema = 'public'
		           AND table_name = 't'
		       ) AS child ON conkey[1] = child.ordinal_position
		  JOIN (
		        SELECT pc.oid,
		               cols.table_schema,
		               cols.table_name,
		               cols.column_name,
		               cols.ordinal_position
		          FROM pg_class AS pc
		          JOIN pg_namespace AS pn ON pc.relnamespace = pn.oid
		          JOIN information_schema.columns AS cols ON (pc.relname = cols.table_name AND pn.nspname = cols.table_schema)
		       ) AS parent ON (
		                       con.confkey[1] = parent.ordinal_position
		                       AND con.confrelid = parent.oid
		                      )
		 WHERE child.column_name != 'rowid';

<---- 
   array
--------------
  {public,t2,w,j}
```

This seems a bit off - shouldn't `is_constraint_active` return true for our FK constraint? we are filtering AllConstraints https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/7a8844145efd224895a873dc752553da1ffd65dc/pkg/sql/catalog/descriptor.go#L633-L643

Well, it turns out `ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT FK` in an explicit txn falls back to the legacy schema changer - which exhibits this behavior. If we set `set use_declarative_schema_changer = unsafe_always;` and force the DSC, we see that `crdb_internal.is_constraint_active` is true during the explicit txn before commit

cc: @rafiss and @fqazi what do you all think of this (starting from https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/119653#issuecomment-1992601082) - is it intentional that `add constraint FK` falls back to legacy schema changer (noob q: where in the code can i find this out?) and would the fix here be to avoid `add constraint FK` in explicit txns in the schemachange workload?

really nice investigation! 

> is it intentional that add constraint FK falls back to legacy schema changer (noob q: where in the code can i find this out?) 
currently, all schema changes in explicit transactions fall back to the legacy schema changer. `use_declarative_schema_changer = unsafe_always` is the way to avoid that, as you did above.

> and would the fix here be to avoid add constraint FK in explicit txns in the schemachange workload?
the schema change workload relies on explicit txns for most operations. i think what we should do is say that we should only have the RSW generate `alter fk` statements when in declarative mode. something like this might work, since we have different `opWeights` for the declarative mode, but make sure to verify that it does in fact do what we want. 
```

index 3bbd51ef22d..1f91586a49a 100644
--- a/pkg/workload/schemachange/schemachange.go

 		}

+		opWeights[alterTableAddConstraintForeignKey] = 0
 		ops := newDeck(workerRng, opWeights...)
 		declarativeOps := newDeck(workerRng, declarativeOpWeights...)
```

also, could you file a bug that demonstrates how `crdb_internal.is_constraint_active` does not work with the legacy `alter fk`, so that we can track it separately? don't think we will prioritize it right away, but good to have that tracked.
oh also, is the `is_constraint_active` filter even needed? what happens if we remove that?
